item.title: U.K. bans goods from occupied West Bank as Israel and U.S. warn of repercussions
item.description: Britain announces a ban on goods from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, prompting warnings of US repercussions and an angry response from Israel.

item.title: Whatever happened to the Taliban threat: 'We will flog the women'?
item.description: IN 2024, the ruling Taliban pledged to use flogging as well as stoning to punish people for not following certain of their precepts — committing adultery, running secret schools for girls. Have they followed through?

item.title: GOP to host unusual midterm convention. And, Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect
item.description: Republicans are aiming to get voters to turn out for the midterms with an unconventional convention. And, Canada's retaliatory tariffs on the U.S. went into effect at midnight.

item.title: Has the economy gone C-shaped?
item.description: A K means the rich and poor are pulling apart. A C supposedly means they're coming back together. We hear the case for both. Which letter you see may depend on what you choose to pay attention to.

item.title: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia ignite fires at oil facilities and wound 73 people
item.description: The attacks come after weeks of escalating clashes between the Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces in Yemen, which shattered a four-year truce in the country's civil war.

item.title: 60 years later, 'Star Trek' continues to 'live long and prosper'
item.description: The television series, Star Trek, turns 60 on Tuesday. The original show aired for only three seasons, but it spawned prequels and sequels (on TV and in theaters) and still has a cult following.

item.title: The 2026 midterm general election season is upon us. Here's what to watch
item.description: The week of Labor Day marks the unofficial kickoff of the general election season. President Trump's unpopularity and Democratic enthusiasm means control of Congress is on the ballot.

item.title: What to know about Canada's escalating trade war with the U.S.
item.description: Canada struck back at U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday with tariffs on about $20 billion worth of U.S. goods. The outcome could resonate far beyond Canada.
